sentences.nl: Welkom bij ‘Heb je zin? – 2’
sentences.en: Welcome to 'Are You in the Mood? - 2'

sentences.nl: Veel dank voor alle positieve commentaren, op mijn vorige reeks van de ‘Heb je zin?’ filmpjes.
sentences.en: Many thanks for all the positive comments on my previous series of 'Are you in the mood?' videos.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Many thanks for all positive comments, on my previous series of the 'Are you in the mood?' videos.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Veel dank" is a common way to express gratitude, similar to "many thanks" in English.  
• "Commentaren" is the plural form of "commentaar," meaning "comments."  
• "Reeks" means "series," and "van de ‘Heb je zin?’ filmpjes" specifies which series is being referred to.

Extra Examples:  
• "Veel dank voor je hulp." (Many thanks for your help.)  
• "Op mijn vorige werk had ik meer vrijheid." (At my previous job, I had more freedom.)  
• "Heb je zin om te gaan zwemmen?" (Do you feel like going swimming?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Veel dank voor de uitnodiging naar je feest." (Many thanks for the invitation to your party.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "Heb je zin?" is commonly used in Dutch to ask if someone is interested or feels like doing something. It's a casual and friendly way to propose activities.

sentences.nl: En omdat jullie het zo graag willen,, is hier een nieuw seizoen van ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: And because you want it so much, here is a new season of 'Heb je zin?'
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And because you all it so gladly want, is here a new season of 'Are you excited?'

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The word "omdat" (because) is a subordinating conjunction, which means it pushes the verb to the end of the clause.  
• "Jullie" is the plural form of "you," used for addressing more than one person.  
• "Zo graag willen" is a phrase meaning "to want something very much," showing a high level of desire.  
• Example 1: "Omdat ik het zo graag wil, ga ik vroeg opstaan." (Because I want it so much, I will get up early.)  
• Example 2: "Zij willen het boek zo graag lezen." (They want to read the book so much.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "En omdat zij het zo graag willen, krijgen ze een extra vrije dag." (And because they want it so much, they get an extra day off.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "Heb je zin?" (Are you excited?) is a common way to express anticipation or eagerness in Dutch. It's often used in informal contexts.

sentences.nl: In ‘Heb je zin?’, oefenen we de grammatica, van mijn #dutchgrammar lessen.

sentences.en: On the website learndutch.org, you will find the text of 'Heb je zin?', the Dutch text and the English translation.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• On the website learndutch.org, find you the text of 'Heb je zin?':, the Dutch text and the English translation.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Op de website" (On the website) uses the preposition "op" to indicate location.  
• "vind je" (find you) follows the Dutch word order where the verb comes first in questions and second in statements.  
• "Heb je zin?" is a common phrase meaning "Are you in the mood?" or "Do you want to?"  

Examples:  
• "Op de tafel ligt een boek." (On the table lies a book.)  
• "Vind je het boek leuk?" (Do you like the book?)  
• "Heb je zin in koffie?" (Are you in the mood for coffee?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Op het bord staat het menu van vandaag. (On the board is today's menu.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Heb je zin?" is often used in casual and friendly contexts to invite someone to participate in an activity, reflecting the informal and direct communication style common in Dutch culture.

sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And pay good attention to the use, of the grammar construction, that we that video discuss.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Let goed op" means "pay attention" and uses the imperative form. "Op" is a preposition that connects with "let" to form a phrasal verb.  
• "Het gebruik" translates to "the use," with "het" being the definite article for neuter nouns.  
• "Die we die video behandelen" means "that we discuss in that video," where "die" is a relative pronoun referring to "constructie" and "video."

Extra phrases:  
• Let op de kinderen. (Pay attention to the children.)  
• Hij let goed op zijn spullen. (He pays good attention to his belongings.)  
• De grammatica die we leren is belangrijk. (The grammar that we learn is important.)

sentences.nl: Ben je benieuwd hoe het verder gaat, met Martin, Marieke, Gianluca, Xing en alle anderen? — Nou, we gaan nu beginnen, met seizoen 2 van ‘Heb je zin?’
sentences.en: Are you curious about how things will continue with Martin, Marieke, Gianluca, Xing, and everyone else? — Well, we're now starting with season 2 of 'Heb je zin?'
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Are you curious how it further goes, with Martin, Marieke, Gianluca, Xing and all others? — Well, we go now start, with season 2 of ‘Are you in the mood?’

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ben je benieuwd" (Are you curious): "Ben" is the first person singular of "zijn" (to be), and "benieuwd" is an adjective meaning curious.  
• "hoe het verder gaat" (how it further goes): "hoe" (how) introduces a subordinate clause, "het" (it) is the subject, "verder" (further) is an adverb, and "gaat" (goes) is the verb.  
• "Nu beginnen" (now start): "nu" (now) is an adverb of time, and "beginnen" (start) is the base form of the verb.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Ben je klaar?" (Are you ready?)  
  - "Hoe gaat het met je?" (How are you doing?)  
  - "We gaan nu eten." (We are going to eat now.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ben je benieuwd wat er volgende week gebeurt?" (Are you curious about what happens next week?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of multiple names in the sentence suggests a storyline or series, which is common in Dutch storytelling media such as radio plays, podcasts, or TV series, where characters are introduced in succession. "Heb je zin?" as a title implies an engaging or entertaining series that draws the audience in.

sentences.nl: Maar voor de mensen, die het eerste seizoen niet hebben gezien,, is hier een korte samenvatting.
sentences.en: But for the people who haven't seen the first season, here is a short summary.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But for the people, who the first season not have seen, is here a short summary.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• **Relative Clause**: "die het eerste seizoen niet hebben gezien" is a relative clause explaining "de mensen". In Dutch, the relative pronoun "die" is used for plural nouns and follows the noun it describes.  
• **Verb Order**: In subordinate clauses like this relative clause, the verbs are placed at the end ("niet hebben gezien").  
• **Word Order**: The main clause begins with "Maar voor de mensen," which sets up the context before the main verb "is," placing emphasis on the following information.

Examples:  
– De boeken, die ik gisteren heb gelezen, waren interessant. (The books, which I read yesterday, were interesting.)  
– De kinderen, die buiten spelen, zijn mijn neven en nichten. (The children, who are playing outside, are my nieces and nephews.)  
– Voor de gasten, die laat arriveren, is er nog eten. (For the guests, who arrive late, there is still food.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Voor de studenten, die de toets niet hebben gemaakt, is er een herkansing. (For the students, who did not take the test, there is a retake.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, providing a summary or recap of a show or event is quite common, especially for TV series where viewers might have missed previous episodes.

sentences.nl: En nu wordt het een beetje gecompliceerd:, Martin vindt Marieke leuk,, maar Gianluca vindt Marieke ook leuk!
sentences.en: And now it gets a bit complicated: Martin likes Marieke, but Gianluca also likes Marieke!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• And now becomes it a bit complicated: Martin finds Marieke nice, but Gianluca finds Marieke also nice!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wordt" is the third person singular form of "worden," meaning "to become."  
• "Vindt" is from "vinden," meaning "to find," but in this context, it is used as "to like" or "to find nice."  
• "Ook" means "also," indicating that Gianluca shares the same opinion.

• Extra examples:  
  - "Het wordt donker." (It is becoming dark.)  
  - "Zij vindt hem aardig." (She finds him nice.)  
  - "Ik hou ook van chocolade." (I also love chocolate.)

## 3. Create a New Example

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, directness is common, and expressing opinions about liking or disliking someone is often straightforward.

sentences.nl: Gianluca en Marieke romantisch dineerden, en… dat Gianluca tegen Xing zei,, dat hij en Marieke samen waren.
sentences.en: Gianluca and Marieke dined romantically, and... Gianluca told Xing that he and Marieke were together.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Gianluca and Marieke romantically dined, and… that Gianluca to Xing said, that he and Marieke together were.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses past tense: "dineerden" (dined) and "zei" (said). Notice the use of "en" (and) to list actions.  
• The phrase "tegen Xing zei" (said to Xing) shows the indirect object placement.  
• "Dat hij en Marieke samen waren" (that he and Marieke were together) is a subordinate clause introduced by "dat" (that).

Examples:  
• "Hij en zijn broer voetbalden, en hij vertelde later dat ze wonnen." (He and his brother played football, and he later said that they won.)  
• "Lisa en Tom dansten de hele nacht, en toen vertelde Lisa dat ze verloofd waren." (Lisa and Tom danced all night, and then Lisa said that they were engaged.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Anna en Peter samen lunchten, en Anna vertelde dat ze een reis plannen." (Anna and Peter lunched together, and Anna said that they are planning a trip.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, indirect communication ("zeggen tegen" - "to say to") is common in storytelling, where details are often shared through conversations with others.

sentences.nl: Xing vertelde dit daarna tegen Martin, en die moest toen erg huilen.
sentences.en: Xing told this to Martin afterwards, and he then cried a lot.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Xing told this afterwards to Martin, and he had then very cry.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vertelde" is the past tense of "vertellen" (to tell). Dutch past tense for regular verbs often adds "-de" or "-te" depending on the verb's ending.  
• "Daarna" means "afterwards" and indicates a sequence of events.  
• "Moest" is the past tense of "moeten" (must/have to), which is used here to indicate that Martin had to cry, implying an emotional response.  
• "Erg" means "very" and is used to intensify the verb "huilen" (to cry).

Examples:  
• Zij vertelde het verhaal aan de klas. (She told the story to the class.)  
• Daarna gingen we naar huis. (Afterwards, we went home.)  
• Hij moest lachen toen hij de grap hoorde. (He had to laugh when he heard the joke.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa vertelde het nieuws aan haar moeder, en die moest toen erg lachen. (Lisa told the news to her mother, and she had to laugh a lot then.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of "moest huilen" to describe an emotional response is common in Dutch storytelling, emphasizing the emotional impact of events.

sentences.nl: Maar gelukkig troostte Xing Martin…, en… ze werden een beetje verliefd op elkaar!
sentences.en: But fortunately, Xing comforted Martin..., and... they fell a little in love with each other!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But fortunately comforted Xing Martin..., and... they became a bit in love with each other!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maar gelukkig" (But fortunately) is a common way to start sentences in Dutch, indicating a contrast with previous information.  
• "Troostte" is the past tense of "troosten" (to comfort), following the regular past tense formation for weak verbs.  
• "Ze werden verliefd op elkaar" translates to "they fell in love with each other". "Werden" is the past tense of "worden" (to become), and "op elkaar" means "with each other".  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij troostte zijn vriend na het slechte nieuws." (He comforted his friend after the bad news.)  
  - "Ze werden boos op elkaar na het misverstand." (They got angry with each other after the misunderstanding.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Maar gelukkig hielp Maria haar broer met zijn huiswerk." (But fortunately Maria helped her brother with his homework.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, expressing emotions like comfort and love tends to be more reserved compared to some cultures. Public displays of affection are generally modest, and comfort is often offered in a practical manner.

sentences.nl: Geef mij maar een beetje een onhandige jongen…, zoals Martin.
sentences.en: Just give me a bit of an awkward guy..., like Martin.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Give me just a little an awkward boy..., like Martin.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Geef mij maar" is an informal way to express preference, often translated as "I'll take" or "I prefer."  
• "Een beetje" means "a little" or "a bit," indicating a small amount or degree.  
• "Onhandige" is an adjective meaning "awkward" or "clumsy." It describes "jongen" (boy) and agrees in form.  
• "Zoals" means "like" or "such as," used to give an example.

• Examples:  
  - "Geef mij maar een kopje koffie." (I'll take a cup of coffee.)  
  - "Een beetje hulp zou fijn zijn." (A little help would be nice.)  
  - "Zo'n onhandige situatie wil ik vermijden." (I want to avoid such an awkward situation.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Geef mij maar een rustige middag aan het strand." (I'll take a quiet afternoon at the beach.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• "Geef mij maar" is a colloquial expression often used in informal settings in the Netherlands to express a preference, indicating a relaxed and straightforward manner of making choices.

sentences.nl: Vandaag, oefenen we de grammatica, van #dutchgrammar-2,, les 4 en 5 over de imperatief;, in andere woorden: ‘de gebiedende wijs’.
sentences.en: Today, we are practicing the grammar from #dutchgrammar-2, lessons 4 and 5 on the imperative; in other words: 'the imperative mood'.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today, practice we the grammar, of #dutchgrammar-2, lesson 4 and 5 about the imperative; in other words: 'the commanding form'.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "vandaag" (today) at the beginning, which is a common way to start a sentence with an adverb of time in Dutch.  
• "Oefenen we" is in the present tense and follows the subject "we" in an inverted order because the sentence begins with an adverb.  
• "De imperatief" (the imperative) is a grammatical term for commands or requests.  
• Example 1: Morgen, gaan we naar het strand. (Tomorrow, we go to the beach.)  
• Example 2: In de ochtend, drink ik koffie. (In the morning, I drink coffee.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Vandaag, koken we het avondeten samen. (Today, we cook dinner together.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch educational contexts, grammar exercises are often structured around specific modules or lessons, which may be referenced by numbers, as seen in the sentence.

sentences.nl: Marieke is op zoek naar Martin,, want Martin heeft Marieke beloofd, om samen romantisch naar de maan te kijken…, op het bruggetje van het vakantiepark, van de Dutch Summer School.
sentences.en: Marieke is looking for Martin, because Martin promised Marieke to romantically watch the moon together on the little bridge of the holiday park of the Dutch Summer School.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke is on search for Martin, because Martin has Marieke promised, to together romantically at the moon to look, on the little bridge of the holiday park, of the Dutch Summer School.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Marieke is op zoek naar Martin" uses "op zoek naar," which means "looking for." This is a common phrase in Dutch.  
• "heeft Marieke beloofd, om samen romantisch naar de maan te kijken" uses the perfect tense ("heeft beloofd") to indicate a completed action or promise. "Om... te kijken" is an infinitive construction often used to express purpose or intention.  
• "op het bruggetje van het vakantiepark" shows possession using "van," similar to "of" in English.  

Examples:  
– "Ik ben op zoek naar mijn sleutels." (I am looking for my keys.)  
– "Hij heeft haar verteld om vroeg te komen." (He told her to come early.)  
– "Het huis van mijn ouders is groot." (The house of my parents is big.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Eva is op zoek naar haar kat, want hij heeft haar beloofd om thuis te blijven." (Eva is looking for her cat because he promised her to stay home.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The Dutch Summer School is a popular way for people to learn Dutch intensively over a short period, often in an immersive environment. It combines language learning with cultural experiences.

sentences.nl: Maar jij hebt toch iets met Gianluca? — Zeg dat toch niet!
sentences.en: But you have something with Gianluca, don't you? — Don't say that!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• But you have still something with Gianluca? — Say that still not!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Maar" is a conjunction meaning "but," often used to contrast ideas.  
• "Toch" is used for emphasis or to express disbelief, similar to "still" or "after all" in English.  
• "Hebt" is the second person singular form of "hebben," which means "to have."  
• "Iets met" translates to "something with," often implying a romantic or significant relationship in Dutch.

Examples:  
• "Maar hij is toch je vriend?" (But he is still your friend?)  
• "Zeg dat toch niet zo hard!" (Don't say that so loudly!)  
• "Je hebt toch geen tijd?" (You still don't have time, do you?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The phrase "iets met iemand hebben" can imply a romantic or special relationship, often used in casual conversations to hint at a connection that may not be explicitly defined.

sentences.nl: Hij is een echte macho.
sentences.en: He is a real macho.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• He is a true macho.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Hij is" is the simple present tense of the verb "zijn" (to be) in the third person singular.  
• "Een" is the indefinite article "a" or "an" in Dutch.  
• "Echte" is an adjective meaning "true" or "real," and it is used here in its base form because it precedes a noun.  
• "Macho" is a borrowed word from Spanish, describing a man who is aggressively masculine.

• Examples:  
  - "Zij is een echte vriendin." (She is a true friend.)  
  - "Dat is een echte Ferrari." (That is a real Ferrari.)  
  - "Hij gedraagt zich als een macho." (He behaves like a macho.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Zij is een echte leider. (She is a true leader.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The term "macho" in Dutch often carries a slightly negative connotation, implying excessive pride in masculinity or a stereotypically tough demeanor.

sentences.nl: Ja, hij maakt leuke complimentjes, maar …, geef mij toch maar een beetje een onhandige jongen.
sentences.en: Yes, he gives nice compliments, but ..., I'd rather have a somewhat awkward guy.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Yes, he makes nice compliments, but ..., give me anyway just a little bit an awkward boy.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Ja" is a straightforward affirmation meaning "yes."  
• "Hij maakt leuke complimentjes" uses "maakt" (makes) as the verb, with "leuke complimentjes" (nice compliments) as the object. "Leuke" is the plural form of "leuk," an adjective meaning nice or fun.  
• "Geef mij toch maar" is an idiomatic expression that means "give me anyway" or "I'd rather have." The phrase implies preference.  
• "Een beetje" means "a little bit," often used to soften statements or add nuance.  
• Example: "Ik drink toch maar een beetje wijn." (I'll just have a little bit of wine anyway.)  
• Example: "Hij maakt vaak grappige opmerkingen." (He often makes funny remarks.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Ja, zij maakt heerlijke taarten, maar geef mij toch maar een simpele cake." (Yes, she makes delicious pies, but I'd rather have a simple cake.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Compliment-giving in Dutch culture can be straightforward, but it's also appreciated when it is genuine and specific. Dutch people often prefer honesty and may find overly gushy compliments less sincere.

sentences.nl: Wees maar niet ongerust.
sentences.en: Don't worry.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Be but not worried.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Wees" is the imperative form of "zijn" (to be).  
• "Maar" is often used to soften commands or make them more friendly.  
• "Ongerust" means worried, with "on-" being a prefix that indicates negation, similar to "un-" in English.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Wees voorzichtig." (Be careful.)  
  - "Wees stil." (Be quiet.)  
  - "Maak je maar geen zorgen." (Don't worry about it.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Wees maar geduldig." (Just be patient.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• The use of "maar" in sentences like this can make directives sound less harsh and more conversational in Dutch.

sentences.nl: Dit is toch de enige avond, dat de docenten alcohol mogen drinken? — Drink maar een lekker glaasje Poolse wodka!
sentences.en: Isn't this the only evening that the teachers are allowed to drink alcohol? — Just enjoy a nice glass of Polish vodka!
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• This is yet the only evening, that the teachers alcohol may drink? — Drink but a nice little glass Polish vodka!

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Dit is toch de enige avond" uses "toch" for emphasis, suggesting an expectation or reminder.  
• "dat de docenten alcohol mogen drinken" is a relative clause explaining conditions related to the evening, with "mogen" indicating permission.  
• "Drink maar een lekker glaasje Poolse wodka!" uses "maar" to soften the imperative, making it more of an invitation than a command.  

Examples:  
- "Het is toch al laat, laten we naar huis gaan." (It is already late, let's go home.)  
- "Je mag maar één koekje nemen." (You may only take one cookie.)  
- "Zij is toch de beste zangeres van de groep." (She is still the best singer of the group.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Dit is toch de beste tijd om naar het strand te gaan." (This is really the best time to go to the beach.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, alcohol consumption is often seen as a social activity, and it's not uncommon for events or gatherings to involve moderate drinking. The sentence suggests a special occasion where teachers are permitted to relax and enjoy themselves.

sentences.nl: Marieke antwoordt: ‘Hmm… Goed idee!’
sentences.en: Marieke replies, ‘Hmm… Good idea!’
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke answers: 'Hmm... Good idea!'

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Antwoordt" is the present tense form of "antwoorden" (to answer). Dutch verbs usually follow the subject directly in the present tense.  
• The sentence includes direct speech, which is set off by quotation marks in both Dutch and English.  
• "Goed idee!" is an exclamatory phrase, simply meaning "Good idea!" in English.

• Extra phrases/sentences:  
  - Hij antwoordt snel. (He answers quickly.)  
  - Dat is een goed plan! (That is a good plan!)  
  - Ze zegt: 'Ja, graag!' (She says: 'Yes, please!')

## 3. Create a New Example

sentences.nl: Anika schenkt de wodka in.
sentences.en: Anika pours the vodka.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Anika pours the vodka in.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Schenkt" is the third person singular form of "schenken," meaning "to pour."  
• "De wodka" uses the definite article "de" for "vodka," which is common for drinks.  
• "In" is a separable prefix in "inschenken," which means "to pour (a drink)." When conjugated, the prefix is separated and placed at the end of the sentence.  
• Example: "Hij schenkt de wijn in." (He pours the wine in.)  
• Example: "Zij schenkt het sap in." (She pours the juice in.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Peter schenkt de koffie in." (Peter pours the coffee in.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it is common to pour drinks for guests as a sign of hospitality.

sentences.nl: Marieke vraagt: ‘Eh… waar zijn jouw huisgenoten?’
sentences.en: Marieke asks, 'Uh... where are your housemates?'
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke asks: 'Uh… where are your housemates?'

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "vraagt" (asks) is in the present tense. In Dutch, present tense is often used for immediate actions or questions.  
• The word "Eh…" is used as a hesitation word, similar to "uh" or "um" in English.  
• "Waar zijn jouw huisgenoten?" uses a typical Dutch question structure, with the verb "zijn" (are) placed before the subject "jouw huisgenoten" (your housemates).

Extra Examples:  
• "Peter vraagt: ‘Hoe laat begint de film?’" (Peter asks: ‘What time does the movie start?’)  
• "Karin zegt: ‘Eh… ik weet het niet.’" (Karin says: ‘Uh… I don’t know.’)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Lisa vraagt: ‘Waar is de supermarkt?’ (Lisa asks: ‘Where is the supermarket?’)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, it’s common to use hesitation words like "eh" during conversations as a way to buy a little time to think, much like in English. It's a casual and informal speech pattern.
